summary: The Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2025 extends and updates federal programs and grants aimed at combating human trafficking both domestically and internationally through fiscal year 2029. It reauthorizes International Megan's Law, establishes support and education programs for victims, adjusts foreign assistance rules, and modifies country evaluation criteria related to human trafficking.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible individuals may receive social services, life-skills training, education, employment support, record expungement assistance, and mental health funding for up to 5 years.
Schools in high-intensity child sex trafficking or labor trafficking areas may receive grant-funded education and training regarding trafficking prevention, grooming, and exploitation.
Required to continue providing specific travel information under International Megan's Law through FY2029.

Subject to updated country ranking criteria on the Tier 2 Watch List and potential withholding of nonhumanitarian, nontrade-related foreign assistance for noncompliance with anti-trafficking standards.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes federal anti-trafficking programs and International Megan's Law through FY2029.
Establishes the Frederick Douglass Human Trafficking Prevention Education Grants to prioritize local educational agencies in high-intensity trafficking areas and provide training.

Creates the Frederick Douglass Human Trafficking Survivors Employment and Education Program through the Department of Health and Human Services to help victims integrate or reintegrate into society over a period of 5 years.
Requires the Department of State's Trafficking in Persons Report to include information regarding trafficking for the purpose of organ removal.
Narrows types of countries listed on the Tier 2 Watch List and adjusts the time a country can remain on the watch list.

Extends authorizations of appropriations for various trafficking programs, including specific funding amounts for housing assistance grants, the National Human Trafficking Hotline, and cybersecurity and public education campaigns.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2025 extends and updates federal programs and grants aimed at combating human trafficking both domestically and internationally through fiscal year 2029. It reauthorizes International Megan's Law, establishes support and education programs for victims, adjusts foreign assistance rules, and modifies country evaluation criteria related to human trafficking.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a broad reauthorization and funding extension of U.S. federal laws addressing domestic and international human trafficking. It updates federal frameworks by adding specific provisions for organ removal trafficking, modifying international watch-list criteria, and introducing targeted education and survivor support programs.
